title: Unscented Kalman Filtering for 3D Orientation Estimation
subtitle: Quaternion UKF with IMU calibration and Vicon ground truth
summary: Implemented a quaternion-based UKF for 3D orientation estimation from raw IMU data, with a full sensor calibration pipeline and Vicon-based evaluation.

glance.oneLiner: Quaternion UKF for IMU-only 3D orientation tracking with Vicon-calibrated sensors.
glance.problem: Estimate 3D orientation from noisy, bias-ridden IMU measurements on a nonlinear rotation manifold, using Vicon ground truth for calibration and evaluation.
glance.approach: Calibrate accelerometer and gyroscope from raw ADC counts, represent orientation as a unit quaternion with covariance in the tangent space, and propagate sigma points through nonlinear dynamics and measurement models.
glance.results: Produces stable orientation estimates that track Vicon ground truth when calibration is correct; highlights the importance of bias/sensitivity estimation and quaternion-aware statistics.
takeaways: Calibration quality dominates downstream orientation accuracy.
Quaternion-aware averaging is essential for consistent UKF updates.
Visualization is critical for diagnosing drift and sign/axis errors.

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: This project implements an Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) to estimate the 3D orientation of a rigid body using raw IMU data. The IMU provides tri-axial accelerometer and gyroscope measurements, while high-accuracy Vicon motion capture data serves as ground truth for calibration and evaluation.

Orientation lives on a non-Euclidean manifold, so the filter uses quaternions and a tangent-space covariance. The dataset provides irregularly sampled IMU readings and synchronized Vicon rotations, which are used to align axes, correct sign conventions, and validate the filter output.

sections.title: Sensor Calibration
paragraphs: Raw IMU measurements arrive as ADC counts, so both accelerometer and gyroscope channels require calibration before filtering. We use a linear calibration model with per-axis bias and sensitivity parameters to map raw counts into physical units.

Accelerometer calibration enforces gravity magnitude consistency and validates roll/pitch against Vicon-derived angles. Gyroscope calibration compares differentiated Vicon orientation with raw angular velocities to estimate bias and scale, which is critical for controlling drift over time.

Calibration parameters are learned on a training sequence and fixed for evaluation on held-out data. This step dominates overall performance and is the most common source of failure when axes or sign conventions are mismatched.

sections.title: Estimation of Rotation
paragraphs: The UKF state is composed of a unit quaternion for orientation and a 3D angular velocity vector. Because quaternions are constrained to unit norm, uncertainty is represented in a 6D tangent space rather than the full 7D state.

Sigma points are generated from the covariance via a matrix square root, mapped into axis-angle perturbations for the quaternion component, and applied through quaternion multiplication. Angular velocity updates are additive in Euclidean space.

To compute the mean orientation, we iteratively average relative quaternion errors in axis-angle form until convergence. This yields a valid mean quaternion and covariance estimate compatible with UKF updates.

The measurement model combines accelerometer-derived gravity direction with gyroscope angular velocity. Sigma points are passed through this model to compute predicted measurement statistics, which drive the Kalman update using cross-covariance terms.

sections.title: Results and Discussion
paragraphs: The filter produces stable orientation estimates that closely track Vicon ground truth when calibration is correct and noise parameters are well tuned. Euler-angle plots are especially useful for spotting axis flips, timing misalignment, or gyro scale errors.

The main sensitivity is calibration quality: small gyroscope scale errors cause rapid drift, while accelerometer bias errors distort gravity alignment. Quaternion-aware averaging and careful uncertainty propagation are essential for consistency on the rotation manifold.
Overall, this project reinforced the importance of geometric state representations, sensor calibration pipelines, and visualization-driven debugging for nonlinear state estimation in robotics.
